name: TX-18
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+29 partisan lean strongly favors Democrats
Incumbent Menefee has large fundraising and outside-spending edge
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 96%
No polling or expert ratings, so uncertainty stays elevated
model.rationale: The district's D+29 lean, Menefee's incumbency and roughly $10.7 million in combined fundraising and outside support against a lightly funded Republican opponent all point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and markets price the race at 96% Democratic. With no polls available, the margin stays near the fundamentals-based estimate with wide uncertainty.
model.watch: Any late polling showing a much narrower margin, or unusually low turnout in a special-adjacent contest, could pull the expected margin down.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Houston-area TX-18 is a heavily Democratic district with a D+29 partisan lean, and Democrat Christian Menefee holds the seat as the incumbent. He has raised about $3.6 million and benefits from roughly $7 million in outside support, while Republican Ronald Whitfield reports little visible fundraising. No outside groups are spending against Menefee.

Prediction markets give Menefee about a 96% chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling, the forecast leans on district fundamentals, which point to a Democratic win by roughly 28 points. The main uncertainty is turnout and the absence of direct polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
